steps.title: Sterilize coverslips and seed cells
steps.instruction: Rinse each 22 × 22 mm glass coverslip three times with dH₂O, then three times with absolute ethanol, air‑dry 20 min under UV in a laminar hood, optionally coat for adhesion, place in a 6‑well plate and add 2 mL growth medium per well; seed cells to the desired confluency following cell‑line specific instructions.

steps.title: Fix cells with 4 % PFA
steps.instruction: In a fume hood add 400 µL of 20 % PFA (stock, catalog 15713‑S) to the 2 mL medium in each well to obtain 4 % final PFA, tilt gently for even spread and incubate 10 min at room temperature (RT). Discard the fixative, wash twice with 2 mL 1× PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) for 5 min each, then leave the sample in 2 mL 1× PBS.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and solutions
steps.instruction: Make all solutions listed below fresh unless noted otherwise; store at the temperatures indicated.

substeps.instruction: 1 × PBS (10 × PBS diluted 1:10): mix 10 mL 10 × PBS with 90 mL dH₂O to 100 mL total.
Permeabilization buffer A (50 mL): 1 × PBS 50 mL, BSA 0.5 % w/v (0.25 g), Triton X‑100 0.5 % v/v (250 µL). Prepare fresh, store 4 °C ≤2 weeks.
Permeabilization buffer B (50 mL): 1 × PBS 50 mL, BSA 0.5 % w/v (0.25 g), Triton X‑100 0.2 % v/v (100 µL). Prepare fresh, store 4 °C ≤2 weeks.
Antibody diluent (50 mL): 1 × PBS 50 mL, BSA 3 % w/v (1.5 g). Prepare fresh.
Tris‑HCl 50 mM, pH 8.0 (100 mL): dissolve 0.606 g Tris base in 60 mL dH₂O, adjust pH to 8.0 with HCl, bring to 100 mL with dH₂O.
Sodium chloride 5 M (10 mL): dissolve 2.922 g NaCl in dH₂O and bring to 10 mL. (Stock concentration 0.292 g mL⁻¹).
APS 10 % w/v (10 mL): dissolve 1 g ammonium persulfate in dH₂O to 10 mL. Store at RT in a desiccator.

Monomer solution (9.4 mL total, store –20 °C ≤2 months):
   • Sodium acrylate stock 0.38 g mL⁻¹ → final 0.086 g mL⁻¹, add 2.25 mL.
   • Acrylamide stock 0.40 g mL⁻¹ (40 %) → final 0.025 g mL⁻¹ (2.5 %), add 0.58 mL.
   • N,N′‑Methylenebisacrylamide stock 0.02 g mL⁻¹ (2 %) → final 0.0015 g mL⁻¹ (0.15 %), add 0.75 mL.
   • Sodium chloride stock 0.292 g mL⁻¹ → final 0.117 g mL⁻¹, add 4 mL.
   • 10 × PBS 1 × , add 1 mL.
   • dH₂O add 0.82 mL.
   Total volume 9.4 mL. Ensure sodium acrylate solution is colorless; discard if yellow.

Gelling solution (200 µL total, prepare on ice, use immediately):
   1. Monomer solution 188 µL.
   2. dH₂O (or 4‑Hydroxy‑TEMPO inhibitor) 4 µL.
   3. TEMED 4 µL (store RT in desiccator).
   4. APS 10 % w/v 4 µL (add just before use). Pipette in this order on ice; vortex briefly. Degas monomer solution beforehand.
Anchoring solution (2 mL fresh): 20 µL Acryloyl‑X‑SE (10 mg mL⁻¹) + 1 980 µL 1 × PBS.

Digestion solution (1.4 mL total, add Proteinase K just before use):
   • Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 50 mM, 1 099 µL.
   • EDTA 10 mM (1 mM final), 140 µL.
   • Triton X‑100 0.5 % v/v, 7 µL.
   • Guanidine HCl 8 M (0.8 M final), 140 µL.
   • Proteinase K 1:100 (8 U mL⁻¹), 14 µL (add immediately before use).
High‑melt agarose 1 % w/v (50 mL): dissolve 0.5 g agarose in 50 mL dH₂O, melt in microwave (800 W, 30 s intervals, swirl, avoid boiling), cool 5–10 min to ≤ 60 °C before use.

steps.title: First immunostaining iteration (primary antibody)
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells with 1 mL permeabilization buffer A for 10 min at RT, then add 100 µL primary antibody diluted in antibody diluent (3 % BSA) at the manufacturer‑recommended concentration; incubate 1 h at RT.

substeps.instruction: a. After primary incubation, wash sequentially with 1 mL permeabilization buffer A (10 min RT), 1 mL 1× PBS (10 min RT), and again 1 mL permeabilization buffer A (10 min RT). Dip dry with paper between washes.

steps.title: First immunostaining iteration (secondary antibody)
steps.instruction: Dilute Alexa Fluor 488‑conjugated goat anti‑mouse secondary antibody 1:200 in antibody diluent (3 % BSA), protect from light, add 100 µL to the coverslip and incubate 1 h at RT in the dark.

substeps.instruction: a. Wash 1 mL permeabilization buffer A (10 min RT, dark), 1 mL 1× PBS (10 min RT, dark), and 1 mL permeabilization buffer A (10 min RT, dark). Dip dry with paper between washes.

steps.title: Iterative immunostaining cycles 2–4
steps.instruction: Repeat the primary‑then‑secondary staining sequence three additional times using the same antibody concentrations; for all permeabilization steps in iterations 2–4 use permeabilization buffer B (0.2 % Triton X‑100).

substeps.instruction: 1. Permeabilize 10 min RT with 1 mL buffer B.
2. Add 100 µL primary antibody solution, incubate 1 h RT.
3. Wash buffer B → PBS → buffer B (1 mL each, 10 min each, dip‑dry).
4. Add 100 µL secondary antibody (1:200 in diluent), incubate 1 h RT in dark.
5. Wash buffer B → PBS → buffer B (1 mL each, 10 min each, dark).

steps.title: Final washes after iteration 4
steps.instruction: Wash the sample once with 1 mL 1× PBS for 10 min at RT (dark) and once with 1 mL dH₂O for 10 min at RT (dark).

steps.title: Anchoring treatment
steps.instruction: Place the coverslip in a fresh 6‑well plate, pipette 150–200 µL anchoring solution onto the cell side, incubate > 6 h at RT (overnight acceptable), then wash 2 × 15 min with 2 mL 1× PBS. Samples may be stored at 4 °C in PBS in the dark until gelation.

steps.title: Prepare parafilm‑mounted coverslip and spacer
steps.instruction: Cut a piece of parafilm 18 mm × 18 mm, apply a drop of super‑glue to the glass side of a 22 × 22 mm coverslip, press the parafilm (paper side up) onto the glue, let dry. Place the parafilm‑mounted coverslip (paper side up) on a 6‑well plate lid or 60 mm Petri dish, remove the paper to expose the clean parafilm surface, and place the in‑house 3D‑printed spacer (opening radius 5 mm, height 350 µm) on the parafilm.

steps.title: Gel casting (polymerization)
steps.instruction: Cool a 2 mL Eppendorf tube on ice, prepare gelling solution (see step 3, do NOT add APS yet). When ready, add 4 µL APS 10 % w/v, vortex briefly, then pipette 70 µL of the complete gelling solution into the centre of the spacer opening. Remove excess PBS from the cell‑coverslip with tissue paper, place the cell‑coverslip (cells facing down) onto the droplet so cells are inside the gel, add a metal hex nut on top, cover with foil and polymerize 30–45 min at RT. Remove the hex nut, flip the sandwich so the parafilm‑mounted coverslip is now on top, discard the parafilm‑coverslip, remove the spacer leaving a circular gel attached to the cell‑coverslip, trim excess gel if needed, and transfer the gel (still on the coverslip, gel side up) to a fresh well of a 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Gel digestion
steps.instruction: Place the gel‑coverslip assembly in a 60 mm Petri dish, add ≥10‑fold excess digestion solution (~2 mL) to fully cover the gel, incubate overnight (≈12 h) at RT in the dark. The gel will detach from the glass; do not peel it off. After digestion, transfer the free gel to a fresh 60 mm dish with a spoon or spatula; discard the original coverslip if detached.

steps.title: Isotropic gel expansion
steps.instruction: Add excess dH₂O (e.g., 20 mL for a 60 mm dish, ≥10× the gel volume) to the digested gel, incubate 1 h at RT in the dark. Carefully discard the water without aspirating the gel, replace with fresh dH₂O and repeat the wash‑replace cycle at least five times until the gel reaches a stable size. After the final wash, measure the expanded gel diameter with a caliper and calculate the expansion factor = post‑expansion diameter ÷ pre‑expansion diameter (pre‑expansion diameter equals the spacer opening, 10 mm).

steps.title: Mount expanded gel for microscopy
steps.instruction: Cut a circular piece of the expanded gel using the 3D‑printed mold, place the gel (mold still attached) onto a new 22 × 22 mm coverslip, insert into an Aireka coverslip cell chamber, lay a 13 mm diameter glass coverslip on top and add a 9 mm hex nut as weight. Pipette ≤1 mL slightly cooled 1 % high‑melt agarose (≤60 °C) into the empty sides of the chamber (avoid entering the gel cavity), then add dH₂O on top of the gel inside the mold to prevent drying. Keep the top coverslip and nut in place during imaging.

steps.title: Confocal image acquisition
steps.instruction: Place the assembled chamber in a standard 35 mm dish holder on the confocal stage, allow temperature to equilibrate, then after 15–30 min acquire images using a water‑immersion objective (e.g., Nikon CFI Plan Apo IR SR 60× WI, NA 1.27, WD 0.17 mm). Record z‑stacks of ~1024 × 1024 pixels with pixel size ≤50–70 nm (x‑y) and ≤200 nm (z) for quantitative analysis.

steps.title: NEDD image denoising (optional)
steps.instruction:
Run the MATLAB NEDD pipeline on the acquired LSCM TIFF stacks. Use the command
   [noisy,denoised,deblurred] = processData(inputPath,outputPath,noiseModel,optionalParams)
where inputPath points to a single‑channel gray‑scale multi‑page TIFF, outputPath is the desired destination, noiseModel is "white" or "colored", and optionalParams is a struct for filter/deconvolution settings. The pipeline estimates noise variance, applies a generalized Anscombe variance‑stabilizing transform, denoises with the RF3D algorithm, inverses the transform, and optionally performs Tikhonov deconvolution.
